topic.title: Michigan Driver Licensing: Permit to License
topic.description: The Michigan adult pathway from eligibility and documents through the Temporary Instruction Permit, knowledge test, third-party road skills test, issuance and renewal — 81 claims verified against official Michigan.gov and SOS sources on 2026-10-04.
topic.focus: 81 verified claims · official Michigan.gov/SOS pages read 2026-10-04 · MCL 257.311, 257.312a

beginner.label: Beginner 🌱
beginner.tagline: The official adult pathway, one step at a time — every rule, fee and deadline below was read from a Michigan.gov or Secretary of State page on 2026-10-04.
goals: Assemble the six document categories for a first-time application, originals only
Run the TIP clock: 30 days supervised practice, 180 days of permit validity
Show up to the road test with the right vehicle papers and know the three components
Read the fee schedule — $25 TIP, $25/$45 first issue, 4-year renewal cycle
Handle the edges: expired license, lost credential, out-of-state transfer, reinstatement

concepts.title: Module 1 — Eligibility and documents (age 18+)
concepts.text:
Who must use this pathway:
Adults 18 or older who have not been licensed in Michigan or any other state in the previous four years must pass a written driver knowledge test and apply for a Temporary Instruction Permit (TIP) at a Secretary of State office — [New drivers age 18 and older](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]. Driver education classes are not required for Michigan residents age 18 and older who apply for a standard or enhanced license. The first application is completed at an office, and applicants pre-apply online while scheduling the visit — the pre-application also shows which documents are required.

Bring one document from each category, plus payment:
- Legal presence (one): valid unexpired US passport or passport card; certified birth certificate from the vital records office showing the registrar certification or seal (a hospital birth certificate is not acceptable); Consular Report of Birth Abroad (FS-240, DS-1350, FS-545); Certificate of Citizenship (N-560 or N-561); Certificate of Naturalization (N-550, N-570, N-578); Permanent Resident Card (I-551); Employment Authorization Document (I-766); or a valid foreign passport with a US visa and entry evidence (F-visa: I-20, J-visa: DS-2019 — B1/B2 and WB/WT stamps not acceptable) — [First-time license or ID](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/first-time-license-or-id) [V 2026-10-04]
- Social Security number (one): Social Security card, W-2 form, SSA 1099, non-SSA 1099, or a pay stub showing name and number; if you are not eligible for an SSN, an SSA-L676 letter of ineligibility
- Identity (one): valid unexpired US passport or passport card; out-of-state, US territory or Canadian license or ID; US-issued name-change document; employee photo ID from a federal or Michigan government agency; CBP Trusted Traveler card; US military photo ID or discharge document; photo ID from a federally recognized Native American tribe; or Michigan DOC prisoner ID — or two of: foreign passport, I-94, Employment Authorization Card, Refugee Travel Document I-571, or expired immigration documents with Form I-797
- Michigan residency (two): utility or credit-card bill issued in the last 90 days (electronic copy accepted), bank or financial account statement issued in the last 90 days, Michigan school report card or transcript, mortgage/lease/rental agreement, pay stub, life/health/auto/home insurance policy, government document, or Michigan title and registration showing the current address — [First-time license or ID](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/first-time-license-or-id) [V 2026-10-04]
- Name-change document if your current name differs, plus payment

Office-visit rules:
- Photocopies of original documents are not accepted, and every document must be in English or carry an English translation
- All documentation is subject to Department of State approval, approval may not come the same day, and an additional visit can be required — [Document requirements](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/license-and-id/license-and-id-document-requirements) [V 2026-10-04]
- Every applicant passes a vision exam at the office visit and has a license photo taken
- Payment at SOS: cash, checks and money orders payable to the State of Michigan, American Express/Discover/MasterCard/Visa credit and debit, plus Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay — a service fee applies to card use

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

concepts.title: Module 2 — Temporary Instruction Permit and the knowledge test
concepts.text:
Getting the permit:
Pass a vision test, pass the written knowledge test (it includes a road-sign test), prove a valid Social Security number or a letter of ineligibility, prove legal presence, identity and Michigan residency, and pay the $25 TIP fee — [New drivers age 18 and older](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]. A TIP is not a license, so driving one without supervision is illegal.

The knowledge test:
- Multiple-choice, covering basic traffic laws and safe vehicle operation, taken at computer stations in SOS offices in English and foreign languages, in audio and written format
- In-office tests can be scheduled up to one hour before closing
- Failing ends that testing session, and the test has to be retaken on a different day after rescheduling
- A passed result stays valid for one year; a new TIP requested after the old one expired means taking the knowledge test again
- Online option for age 18+: the identical test on a computer with keyboard, mouse and webcam, with random photos taken for proctoring; the Operator section runs about 45 minutes and the Signs segment about 15 minutes; the online test costs $6.50 including convenience and card-processing fees, while the in-office test has no fee
- Suspended, revoked or denied drivers are ineligible and get no refund if they attempt the online test; after passing online, an SOS office visit is still required to receive the TIP

Supervised practice before the road test:
- Current rule: adults must first be issued a TIP and complete at least 30 days of supervised driving before they may take the driving skills test
- TIPs are valid for 180 days from the date issued; if the skills test is not passed inside that window the whole process restarts and a new TIP application must be submitted at an SOS office
- Practice driving must be supervised by a validly licensed adult driver, such as a family member, friend or co-worker, or done through a driver education provider — the official adult page states no minimum age for the supervising adult
- Optional adult driver education is limited; SOS publishes a list of state-certified providers offering adult courses

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

concepts.title: Module 3 — Road skills test
concepts.text:
Who runs the test:
Michigan's driving skills tests are given entirely by independent driver testing businesses authorized by the Michigan Department of State, whose examiners conduct them, and SOS does not regulate the fees these businesses charge — [New drivers age 18 and older](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]. No official statewide price range for the road test is published, so treat any dollar range you see as unverified and get quotes.

Before you schedule:
- Ask each testing business about all of its fees, including initial and retest fees, refund policies, charges for improper documents, defective equipment and failure to keep an appointment
- Find testers through the SOS county search called Locate a driver testing business

What the test covers:
- It takes about 45 minutes to an hour and a half and has three components: vehicle inspection, basic control skills test, and on-the-road driving test
- The skills-test route contains a variety of traffic situations including city, residential and expressway driving, and the study guide table of contents also lists Expressway or Rural Highway plus Urban and Residential Areas — [Driving Skills Test Study Guide (PDF)](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/01preston/Driving-Skills-Test-Study-Guide.pdf) [V 2026-10-04]
- Present to the examiner: your TIP, a vehicle in safe working order, proof of Michigan No-Fault insurance, and the vehicle registration with a license plate carrying the correct year's tab
- The examiner inspects the vehicle before any testing, and a vehicle that does not meet legal or safety standards cancels the test — unsafe or defective parts such as a broken signal light or missing side-view mirror cannot be used

After a pass:
- The examiner issues a signed Driving Skills Test receipt, which is not a license, and the business reports the result electronically
- Once results post, sign in to e-Services for a Temporary Operator License to drive while the permanent license is processed and mailed; if results are not posted within 24 hours, take the skills test certificate, the TIP and identification to an SOS office

Statute for carrying the credential:
- MCL 257.311 requires a licensee to have an operator's or chauffeur's license, or the receipt described in section 311a, in immediate possession at all times when operating a motor vehicle, and to display it on demand — this is the rule for why the TIP and receipts are carried, not a testing rule — [MCL 257.311](https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-257-311) [V 2026-10-04]

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

concepts.title: Module 4 — After you pass: issuance and renewal
concepts.text:
Issuance and cost:
- A standard driver's license costs $25 and an enhanced driver's license costs $45; applicants who meet every requirement are issued a REAL ID-compliant license unless they opt out — REAL ID has been in effect for domestic air travel since May 7 2025 — [New drivers age 18 and older](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Once the skills test is passed the license is processed and mailed; applicants under 21 receive a vertical license marked Under 21, printed and mailed within 10-14 days of application, while applying within 54 days of the 21st birthday yields the horizontal format instead
- Residents with temporary legal presence in the US receive a limited-term license valid only as long as they are authorized to remain in the country

Probation:
- Every newly licensed driver, regardless of age, is placed on probation for a minimum of three years; the last 10 months must pass without an at-fault or had-been-drinking crash, a license suspension or a traffic conviction, or probation is extended — [New drivers age 18 and older](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]

Term and renewal cycle:
- A standard license expires every 4 years on the birthday; renewal opens up to 1 year before expiration and remains possible up to 4 years after expiration, with late fees
- Renewal can be done online, by mail or at self-service stations, and an in-person office visit for a photo and vision test is required about every 12 years — [License or ID renewal](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-or-id-renewal) [V 2026-10-04]
- Renewal fees: standard license $18, standard late renewal $25, enhanced license $38, enhanced late renewal $45, standard ID $10, enhanced ID $30, plus a $4.25 per-item service fee at self-service stations

Statute note:
- MCL 257.312a is motorcycle-indorsement text in the excerpt published by the legislature and supports only the four-year maximum term: a license must not be issued for a period longer than 4 years — [MCL 257.312a](https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-257-312a) [V 2026-10-04]
- The three-year probation rule comes from the official adult page, not from MCL 257.312a

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

concepts.title: Module 5 — Under-18 GDL ladder (compact)
concepts.text:
The ladder:
- Drivers under 18 go through the Graduated Driver Licensing system: two education segments (Segment 1 and Segment 2) and three licensing levels — Level 1 Learner's, Level 2 Intermediate and Level 3 Full — and GDL ends when the teen turns 18 — [New drivers under 18](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18) [V 2026-10-04]
- Level 1 starts at age 14 years and 9 months: complete Segment 1 and pass the Segment 1 state exam, apply with a parent or guardian at an SOS office and pay the $25 licensing fee for a hard card Level 1 license
- At Level 1 the teen may drive only with a parent, guardian or a designated licensed adult age 21 or older, and the designated adult must carry the signed authorization letter from the parent or guardian
- Level 1 must be held for at least six months, Segment 2 must be passed and the required supervised practice hours completed before the on-road skills test; Level 2 requires age 16 plus 90 days crash- and violation-free before issuance, and the GDL level then updates automatically in SOS systems — [First-time license or ID](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/first-time-license-or-id) [V 2026-10-04]
- A Level 1 license expires when the teen turns 18, after which the adult pathway applies; teens holding a valid Level 2 or Level 3 license are automatically issued an operator's license before the 18th birthday — vertical, marked Under 21 and expiring on the 21st birthday
- Kelsey's Law prohibits teen drivers with a GDL Level 1 learner's license from using a cell phone while driving, and Michigan otherwise bans cell phone use while driving except in emergencies or where hands-free technology is allowed

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

concepts.title: Module 6 — Reinstatement, replacement and out-of-state transfer
concepts.text:
Moving to Michigan:
- Bring your current out-of-state driver's license, proof of a valid Social Security number, US citizenship or legal presence if you are not a US citizen, identity, and at least two Michigan residency documents; you are given a vision test and the out-of-state license is converted — documentation is subject to approval and may require an additional visit — [Transfer an out-of-state license](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/license-and-id/new-drivers) [V 2026-10-04]
- New Michigan residents must apply as soon as they establish residency, because Michigan law provides no grace period: “There is no grace period provided in Michigan law”, and a written test is not required when converting a valid out-of-state license — you still take a vision test and have your photo taken — [New Michigan residents](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/resources/communities/new-mi-residents) [V 2026-10-04], [Resident FAQ](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/resources/new-michigan-residents) [V 2026-10-04]

Expired or out of state:
- Renewal stays possible up to 4 years after the expiration date with late fees; a license expired more than four years, or never licensed, means starting the whole TIP process over — [License or ID renewal](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-or-id-renewal) [V 2026-10-04]
- If you are out of state when your license expires, SOS provides a driver's license extension that is valid for 180 days after the date the license expires, mailed on request or obtained through online services; if you are not back within those 180 days, SOS sends renewal-by-mail information instead — [License or ID renewal](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-or-id-renewal) [V 2026-10-04]

Replacing a lost or stolen credential:
- Replace online through e-Services if you have a valid Social Security number and the credential is not expired or canceled — [Replace a license, ID or permit](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-id-or-permit-replacement) [V 2026-10-04]
- While out of state, mail or fax the Duplicate Driver's License Application to the Internal Services Section, 7064 Crowner Drive, Lansing MI 48918, fax 517-636-5865, and a temporary permit comes back with the replacement
- A self-service station also prints a temporary credential, and an office visit takes about 20 minutes on average
- Duplicate fees per SOS form BDVR162: standard operator $9, chauffeur $18, enhanced operator $24, enhanced chauffeur $33, state ID $10, enhanced state ID $30 — [BDVR162 fee schedule (PDF)](https://michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/28lawensn/BDVR162__0903.pdf) [V 2026-10-04]

Reinstatement:
- Fees per SOS form BDVR162: standard $125, Minor in Possession $125, watercraft $125, snowmobile $125 and friend of the court $85; if a reinstatement fee is due, the current Michigan credential is not valid — [BDVR162 fee schedule (PDF)](https://michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/28lawensn/BDVR162__0903.pdf) [V 2026-10-04]
- Pay online with the Pay Reinstatement Fee service, by mail using the driver's license reinstatement application with the card by fax, or at an SOS office with cash, check, money order or card — reinstatement fees are not payable at self-service stations — [License reinstatement fee](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-reinstatement-fee) [V 2026-10-04]
- Clean Slate to Drive: more than 100 violations qualify for termination, including suspensions for failing to pay a ticket or court fee, and clinic fine and fee sponsorship is not guaranteed — [Road to restoration clinics and Clean Slate to Drive laws](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/license-and-id/road-to-restoration-clinics-and-clean-slate-to-drive-laws) [V 2026-10-04]

Booking the office visit:
- Office and knowledge-test visits are scheduled through the SOS appointment system that official pages link to — [Schedule an appointment online (TAP)](https://dsvsesvc.sos.state.mi.us/TAP/?Link=APPOINTMENT) [V 2026-10-04]

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

concepts.title: Module 7 — Costs table
concepts.text:
Every fee with its official source:
- Temporary Instruction Permit (TIP) — $25 — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Written knowledge test at an SOS office — no fee — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Written knowledge test online (age 18+) — $6.50 including convenience and card-processing fees — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Standard driver's license (first issue) — $25 — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Enhanced driver's license (first issue) — $45 — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Road skills test at a third-party driver testing business — set by the business, SOS does not regulate it, and no official price range is published — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Standard license renewal — $18 — [License or ID renewal](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-or-id-renewal) [V 2026-10-04]
- Standard license late renewal — $25 — [License or ID renewal](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-or-id-renewal) [V 2026-10-04]
- Enhanced license renewal — $38, late $45 — [License or ID renewal](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-or-id-renewal) [V 2026-10-04]
- Standard / enhanced state ID renewal — $10 / $30 — [License or ID renewal](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-or-id-renewal) [V 2026-10-04]
- Self-service station service fee — $4.25 per item — [License or ID renewal](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/license-or-id-renewal) [V 2026-10-04]
- GDL Level 1 licensing fee (teens) — $25 — [New drivers under 18](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18) [V 2026-10-04]
- Duplicate / replacement operator license — $9 — [BDVR162 fee schedule (PDF)](https://michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/28lawensn/BDVR162__0903.pdf) [V 2026-10-04]
- Driver's license reinstatement (standard) — $125 — [BDVR162 fee schedule (PDF)](https://michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/28lawensn/BDVR162__0903.pdf) [V 2026-10-04]
- Credit or debit card use at SOS — a service fee is charged, and the amount varies by the processor — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- REAL ID conversion — no added charge for converting to REAL ID if you do so at the time of renewing or replacing your license or ID; otherwise there is a correction fee ($9 for a license and $10 for an ID) — [REAL ID](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/real-id) [V 2026-10-04]
- Free-of-charge license statement — an official SOS release says adults who pass the road test before their TIP expires receive the driver's license free of charge (SOS, July 2 2025), which sits alongside the same page's $25 standard-license price — [SOS news release](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/resources/news/2025/07/02/michigan-secretary-of-state-now-offers-online-drivers-license-testing-for-adults) [V 2026-10-04]

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

concepts.title: Module 8 — Pitfalls and test-day rules
concepts.text:
Test day:
- Bring the TIP, proof of Michigan No-Fault insurance, the vehicle registration, license plate and current-year tab, and a roadworthy vehicle — an unsafe or defective vehicle such as a broken signal light or a missing side-view mirror cancels the test before it starts
- No study aids or notes, no cell phone and no other electronic device during the test; driver-activated features and systems such as parking assist, four-way cameras and automated steering are not allowed — ask the examiner if you are unsure
- Failing any one of the three components (vehicle inspection, basic controls, on-the-road) automatically terminates the skills test; a new appointment is required, and only one driving skills test may be taken in a 24-hour period

Documents:
- Photocopies of original identification documents are rejected, documents must be in English or translated, approval can take an extra visit, and residency documents must be dated within the last 90 days with a Michigan residential address — [First-time license or ID](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/first-time-license-or-id) [V 2026-10-04]
- Your residential address must be a verified US Postal Service street address — [Licenses and IDs FAQ](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/license-and-id/licenses-and-id) [V 2026-10-04]

Clocks that bite:
- Failing the knowledge test ends that session, a passed result expires after one year, and an expired TIP means taking the knowledge test again
- Taking the paid online test while suspended, revoked or denied yields no refund and no license
- The TIP's 180-day clock is absolute: missing it means re-applying, re-paying the $25 fee and restarting supervised practice
- Pre-apply online before the office visit, and remember in-office knowledge tests can only be scheduled up to one hour before closing
- A ticket or an at-fault crash in the final 10 months of the three-year probationary period extends probation

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

concepts.title: Module 9 — Free study resources
concepts.text:
Free official material:
- What Every Driver Must Know (form SOS-133), current edition October 2025, free PDF in English, Spanish, Arabic, Chinese, Dari, French, Pashto, Swahili and Vietnamese — [What Every Driver Must Know](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/resources/forms/what-every-driver-must-know) [V 2026-10-04]
- SOS directs knowledge-test applicants to that manual, especially chapters 4-7, and to the Driving Skills Test Study Guide; both are free from the official page — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Driving Skills Test Study Guide (SOS-360), free PDF — [Driving Skills Test Study Guide (PDF)](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/01preston/Driving-Skills-Test-Study-Guide.pdf) [V 2026-10-04]
- The Supervised Driving Guide (SOS-191), a free coaching manual for supervising adults, is linked from the same page
- Official search tools: Locate a driver testing business (county search) and Locate a driver education provider (state-certified providers)

Taking the test online:
- The official online knowledge test for age 18+ runs through know2drive.michigan.gov, costs $6.50 and is webcam-proctored; no free official practice test was found on Michigan.gov/SOS pages reviewed on 2026-10-04, so free prep means the manual plus the study guide — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- If the online test breaks during proctoring or identity verification, the third-party online-test vendor supports it at 833-939-2364 or MIK2DOnlineSupport@itidmv.com — [New drivers 18+](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older) [V 2026-10-04]
- Office and knowledge-test visits run on the SOS appointment system — [Schedule an appointment online (TAP)](https://dsvsesvc.sos.state.mi.us/TAP/?Link=APPOINTMENT) [V 2026-10-04]

⚠ Verified 2026-10-04 against official Michigan.gov/SOS sources

examples.title: Scenario A — the 180-day TIP clock is about to run out
examples.scenario: An adult passed the knowledge test and got a TIP in April, but work and weather pushed the road test out. Six months later the skills test still has not been taken.
examples.outcome: The TIP expired at 180 days from the date issued, so the whole process restarts: a new TIP application at an SOS office, another $25, and the 30-day supervised driving requirement starts again. Passing inside the window is what keeps the first attempt alive.

examples.title: Scenario B — moving from another state
examples.scenario: Someone establishes residency in Michigan with a valid Ohio license in their wallet and wonders how long they can drive on the old one.
examples.outcome: There is no grace period in Michigan law: apply as soon as residency is established. Bring the out-of-state license, Social Security proof, identity, legal presence if needed, and two residency documents; a vision test and photo are taken, and no written test is required when converting a valid out-of-state license.

examples.title: Scenario C — the license is lost while traveling
examples.scenario: A Michigan licensee realizes the wallet is gone while staying out of state, with no way to visit an office.
examples.outcome: Replace online through e-Services if the credential is not expired, or mail/fax the Duplicate Driver's License Application to the Internal Services Section in Lansing and a temporary permit comes back with the replacement. Back home, a self-service station prints a temporary credential, and an office visit averages about 20 minutes.

pitfalls: MYTH: “I can drive alone now that I have a TIP.” A TIP is not a license — practice driving must be supervised by a validly licensed adult driver or run through a driver education provider, and driving unsupervised is illegal.
MYTH: “The state sets the road-test price.” SOS does not regulate third-party skills-test fees and publishes no statewide range; ask each business about initial AND retest fees before booking.
The TIP's 180-day window is absolute — miss it and the process restarts with a new application, a new $25 fee and a fresh supervised-practice period.
Reinstatement fees are not payable at self-service stations — use the online Pay Reinstatement Fee service, mail with the reinstatement application and card by fax, or pay at an office.
REAL ID is free only when you convert while renewing or replacing; otherwise the correction fee is $9 for a license and $10 for an ID.
Photocopies are rejected and residency documents must be dated within the last 90 days — bring originals of everything in the categories above.
Probation runs three years for every new driver, and a ticket or at-fault crash in the final 10 months extends it.
exercises: List the six document categories for a first-time application and mark which two you would use for Michigan residency.
Count the days: if a TIP is issued on day zero, write the last day the road skills test can be taken, then set a practice schedule that clears the 30-day supervised minimum with room to spare.
Price a road test by calling two driver testing businesses in your county and asking for initial fee, retest fee and refund policy before you book.

glossary.definition: Temporary Instruction Permit — the supervised-practice permit issued after vision, knowledge test and $25 fee; valid 180 days and never a stand-alone license.
The multiple-choice written test on traffic laws, safe operation and road signs taken at an SOS computer station or online for age 18+; a pass stays valid one year.
The third-party driving test: vehicle inspection, basic control skills and on-the-road driving, about 45 minutes to an hour and a half.
The learner's stage of the Graduated Driver Licensing system, starting at age 14 years and 9 months with Segment 1 passed and a parent or guardian present.
The federal standard credential; free to convert while renewing or replacing, otherwise a $9 license or $10 ID correction fee applies.
A minimum three-year clean period for every newly licensed driver; the last 10 months must pass without an at-fault crash, suspension or conviction.
Paying the fee that restores a suspended or revoked credential — $125 standard per form BDVR162 — online, by mail with the reinstatement form, or at an office.
Unattended SOS kiosk handling renewals and printing a temporary credential on replacement, with a $4.25 per-item service fee.

beginner.q: How long must an adult applicant hold a Temporary Instruction Permit and drive under supervision before taking the driving skills test?
options: At least 90 days of supervised driving
At least 30 days of supervised driving
At least 7 days of supervised driving
There is no supervised-driving waiting period
beginner.explain: The official adult page states that adults must first be issued a TIP and complete at least 30 days of supervised driving before they may take the driving skills test.

beginner.q: How long is a Temporary Instruction Permit valid from the date it is issued?
beginner.explain: TIPs are valid for 180 days; if the driving skills test is not passed inside that window the whole process restarts with a new TIP application at an SOS office. A passed knowledge test result, by contrast, stays valid for one year.

beginner.q: What does a Temporary Instruction Permit cost in Michigan?
beginner.explain: The TIP fee is $25. The $6.50 figure is the online knowledge test, $45 is a first-issue enhanced license, and the in-office knowledge test itself carries no fee.

beginner.q: Besides your TIP, which vehicle documents must be present for the road skills test?
options: The vehicle title and a bill of sale
Current insurance only — registration is checked at the office later
Proof of Michigan No-Fault insurance, the vehicle's registration, and a license plate with the correct year's tab
Nothing, because the examiner pulls records from the state system
beginner.explain: The examiner checks a valid certificate of Michigan No-Fault insurance, vehicle registration and a license plate with the correct year's tab, and inspects the vehicle before any testing — a vehicle that fails the inspection cancels the test.

beginner.q: How many components does the driving skills test have, and how long does it take?
options: Three components, about 45 minutes to an hour and a half
One component, an open drive with no inspection
beginner.explain: The test has three components — vehicle inspection, basic control skills and on-the-road driving — and runs about 45 minutes to an hour and a half. Failing any one component terminates the test, so a new appointment is required and only one skills test may be taken in 24 hours.

beginner.q: What are the first-issue fees for a standard and an enhanced Michigan driver's license?
beginner.explain: First issue is $25 for a standard license and $45 for an enhanced license. $18 and $38 are standard and enhanced renewal prices, while $6.50 is the online knowledge test.

beginner.q: What is the minimum age to apply for a GDL Level 1 learner's license?
beginner.explain: Level 1 begins at age 14 years and 9 months, with Segment 1 completed and passed, a parent or guardian present at the office, and the $25 licensing fee paid. Level 2 still requires age 16 plus a 90-day clean record.

beginner.q: Which channels can replace a lost or stolen Michigan license?
options: By mail only, and only from inside Michigan
Replacement is not possible once a license has been issued
In person at an office only
Online through e-Services, by mail or fax while out of state, at a self-service station, or in person at an office
beginner.explain: The replacement page lists online service, mail or fax while out of state (temporary permit included), self-service stations (which print a temporary credential) and office visits averaging about 20 minutes; the duplicate operator license fee is $9.

beginner.q: A standard Michigan license expires every 4 years on the birthday, and renewal opens up to one year before expiration.
beginner.explain: A standard license runs a 4-year cycle; renewal opens up to 1 year before expiration and remains possible up to 4 years after it, with late fees. An in-person photo and vision visit is required about every 12 years.

beginner.q: Converting to REAL ID costs extra even when you do it at the time of renewing your license.
beginner.explain: There is no added charge for converting to REAL ID if you do so at the time of renewing or replacing your license or ID. Otherwise a correction fee applies: $9 for a license, $10 for an ID.
